summary: Atlas Payments requests audit evidence of regional failover actions (who/what/why/when) for enterprise compliance
description:
Customer (Atlas Payments, enterprise) request:

Atlas Payments Security/Compliance team is asking for audit evidence of all routing/failover actions during regional impairment, specifically:
- When Redwood initiated a regional failover / traffic shift (or recommended one)
- Whether it was automated vs. manually approved
- The evidence/signals used (reachability/5xx burn/tail latency/capacity)
- Who approved/executed the action (user/service identity)
- When rollback occurred and why
- Retention period and how Atlas Payments can retrieve evidence for internal audits (SOC2 controls / change management)

Context:
- They noticed transient routing behavior during the planned controlled failover window (mid-Jan) and want an audit trail to attach to their internal change record.
- They also want a forward-looking answer: how Redwood will provide audit logs for future regional events.

Impact:
- No ongoing production outage. Compliance gating: customer has an internal deadline to finalize their Q1 control evidence package.

Ask from Support:
- Provide a customer-ready explanation of the failover audit event format and what evidence we can provide today.
- Confirm retention (default vs. extended) and delivery method (CSV export / API / Console).
- Clarify boundaries: what gets logged at control-plane/routing policy level vs. DNS/provider-level steering.

Notes:
- Customer specifically asked whether we can include the "why" fields (trigger sources) and tie to dashboards/incident timeline.

Requested delivery:
- Written response + sample redacted event(s) from a recent controlled test (acceptable to redact tenant identifiers).
- Confirmation that audit events include rollbacks and anti-flap decisions.
comments: 2026-01-16 09:12 PT — Owen Phillips (Support Incident Liaison): Created per Atlas Payments email follow-up. They want evidence of failover actions + retention statement. Assigning to Dev Patel for customer-facing response; looping in Allison Grant / Miles Thornton for correctness.

2026-01-16 10:03 PT — Dev Patel (Support Escalation Owner): Acknowledged. I’ll draft customer response with:
1) what we log today (recommendations/executions/rollbacks)
2) example record (redacted)
3) retention + access path
4) limitations (DNS/provider routing outside of policy engine). Requesting eng confirmation on final event schema fields and retention defaults.

2026-01-16 11:28 PT — Miles Thornton (Failover architecture lead): Audit event stream is in place for controller decisions. It emits structured events for:
- failover.recommended
- failover.executed
- failover.rollback
Includes policy_id, from_region, to_region, reason_category, evidence summary, and actor (service + optional human approver). See PR-19824. We can provide a redacted sample from the 2026-01-15 controlled test.
Caveat: DNS-level behavior is separately observable; not all provider-side traffic steering is captured as an audit event unless it results in a policy change we own.

2026-01-16 12:10 PT — Allison Grant (Observability lead): Retention: audit events are stored in the central event store (default 30 days) and copied into our compliance archive for enterprise accounts (90 days) upon request/contract addendum. For Atlas we can offer 90 days as a best-effort now; longer retention requires account-level enablement and cost approval. Access: today = Support-provided export; Console export is planned but not yet generally available.

2026-01-16 13:02 PT — Dev Patel: Confirming with Security guidance re: what customer can receive (PII/tenant identifiers). Also need to ensure sample includes only their tenant + any shared infrastructure identifiers are generalized.

2026-01-17 08:40 PT — Dev Patel: Drafted response for Atlas Payments. Key points:
- We generate a failover audit trail whenever automation recommends/executes/rolls back a routing policy change.
- Events include timestamp, environment, affected route/model group, source/target regions, decision type, evidence summary, and actor/approver.
- We can provide a redacted export for the 2026-01-15 controlled test and any subsequent routing changes affecting their traffic.
- Retention: 30 days standard; enterprise retention options available (90+ days) depending on enablement.
- Limitations: provider-side DNS/anycast propagation time is not itself an “audit action” but we can include correlating metrics and change tickets.
Sharing with Miles/Allison for final review before sending.

2026-01-17 10:15 PT — Victor Alvarez (Network reachability lead): Add one sentence that we can correlate to network reachability probes (cross-region) which are part of evidence signals; but DNS TTL/propagation is best-effort and varies by resolver. We don’t guarantee per-client steering timelines beyond our SLO measurement methodology.

2026-01-17 11:06 PT — Dev Patel: Sent customer response via email with:
- 1-page explanation
- sample event (redacted)
- retention statement
- offer to set up recurring export during Q1 while Console self-serve export is being finalized.
Asked customer to confirm whether 90-day retention meets their audit requirement; offered longer retention discussion via CSM.

2026-01-22 15:34 PT — Dev Patel: Customer replied: 90-day retention is acceptable for now; requested one more export covering 2026-01-15 00:00–06:00 PT with all rollback events included. Coordinating with Allison to generate export.

2026-01-23 09:20 PT — Allison Grant: Generated export from event store for the requested window. Includes recommendation + execution + rollback entries and actor/approver fields. Redacted internal hostnames; kept policy IDs and regions. Provided to Dev for delivery.
2026-01-24 10:05 PT — Dev Patel: Delivered export + short readme to Atlas Payments. They confirmed receipt and that it satisfies their internal change record. Marking Resolved.
resolution: Provided customer-ready documentation of failover audit events (recommend/execute/rollback), delivered a redacted export for the controlled failover window, and confirmed retention/access path for enterprise accounts (30 days default; 90 days enabled for Atlas Payments via Support-provided exports pending self-serve Console export).
internal_notes: If Atlas asks for >90 day retention or direct API delivery, route to Product (PM-513 for SLO reporting + auditability expectations) and Security/Compliance for contract/compliance archive enablement. Ensure no cross-tenant identifiers in exports. Tie future requests to PR-19824 schema and incident-bot summaries (PR-412) for timeline correlation.
